subject: fix(interactive): make a list row a row, and put the cursor on it
instruction:
fix(interactive): make a list row a row, and put the cursor on it

`interactive.list` answered with `State.public/1` — the whole session, retained
event window and turn ledger included — for every session, from every fleet
node, on every refresh. A client that wanted one integer, the contiguous
high-water mark, to know whether it had replayed everything, paid for a
transcript to learn it (H1).

`State.summary/1` is the row contract: the same struct, the same `_struct` tag
and the same field names, with `events` and `turns` emptied and `usage` reduced
to `%{total_tokens, cost_usd}` — `nil` for either figure no provider reported,
never a zero that reads as "this was free". `cursor` is on it, as are the title
and `title_source` from the rename slice and `forked_from`/`forks` from the
fork slice, so a picker can draw a name, a position, a spend, and a lineage
without opening anything. `options.capabilities` stays, because that is what a
footer greys its verbs from.

Nothing is lost, only moved: everything a row drops is one `interactive.info`
away, addressed by the id the row already carries.

Acceptance. These tests are restored into the worktree after the session ends and must pass:
  - a row carries title, cursor, and a usage summary, and no event window
  - an unspent session reports no tokens rather than a zero that reads as free
  - a fork's parentage is visible from the list without opening either session

Rules. Files that already exist under `test/` must not be modified or deleted — the change is graded against tests restored from the history after the session ends, applied to a fresh checkout of the starting commit. New test files of your own are allowed and are left in place, but they are yours: they are not copied into the tree the grade runs in. The change is collected as a diff over `lib/`, `assets/`, `priv/`, `config/`, `docs/` and `README.md`; a change to any other path — `mix.exs` and `.formatter.exs` included — is refused rather than graded. Work only inside this worktree.
